content:
# Before you start

This **user guide for the system** *Shadow of the Demon Lord* for *Encounter+* contains **no game rules**: it explains how the system works, not how to play the game.

### What is inside

Three parts, for three uses.

###### The parts of the module

| Part | For whom | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| **Character sheet** | Players and GMs | Creation, level up, play: what the sheet offers, calculates and remembers. |
| **GM side** | GMs | The character card, the creature views, the combat tracker, initiative and the system settings. |
| **Entity index** | Authors | One page per entity: the fields, what they do, what the character sheet imports or calculates on its own. |

### Before you play

::: {.regles .cadre}
- The system and the interactive sheet need ***Encounter+* 5.2 or later**.
- Languages, afflictions and actions are **Rule** entities in your library: the sheet reads them, it does not contain them (see [Prepare your library](prepare)).
- The starting tables (resources, interesting things) are **Table** entities to create or import.
:::

### PDF for your players

The **Character sheet** part also exists as a **PDF** for your players: **Help_SotDL_players.pdf**. It covers the overview, creation, level up, play, and damage, afflictions and rest. It can be [downloaded from the module's GitHub](https://github.com/BriocheMasquee/sotdl-help/releases/latest/download/Help_SotDL_players.pdf).
name: Before you start

content:
## The system at a glance

The system works with **entity types**: eleven types, each with its own form (except Table, which is native to Encounter+).

###### Entity types

| Type | Used for | Index page |
|---|---|---|
| Character | A player character, with an interactive sheet. | [Character](index-character) |
| Creature, NPC | An adversary, an ally or a neutral character. | [Creature and NPC](index-creature) |
| Ancestry | A people and its characteristics. | [Ancestry](index-ancestry) |
| Path | The specializations by level (novice, expert, master). | [Path](index-path) |
| Transformation | A permanent or temporary change in the nature of the character. | [Transformation](index-transformation) |
| Item | Weapon, armor, gear, potion, relic, special item. | [Item](index-item) |
| Spell | A magic spell. | [Spell](index-spell) |
| Complication | A complication in the PC's story. | [Complication](index-complication) |
| Vehicle | Machine, ship or war machine. | [Vehicle](index-vehicle) |
| Rule | Language, affliction, action, state, source… | [Rule](index-rule) |
| Table | A random table. | [Table](index-table) |

### How data moves

::: {.regles .cadre}
- A **Character** receives a **copy** of its ancestry, paths, transformation and complication: editing the form of the original entity does not change the data already imported into an existing character.
- **Rules** (languages, afflictions, actions, states) are read live from the library.
- A **link** in a text connects one entity to another: see [Links and rolls](index-links-dice).
:::
name: The system at a glance

content:
## Credits and notices

### Why this module

The *Shadow of the Demon Lord* system for *Encounter+* is complete, and therefore dense: nested forms, an interactive sheet, GM cards. This module was born from a simple need: **finding your way around without digging into the code**. It aims to be short, checked against the system itself, and free of any game text.

### Author

**Brioche Masquée**: the *Encounter+* “sotdl” system, the interactive sheet, the GM cards, the help modules.

::: {.regles .cadre}
- **Contact**: private message on Discord (**pacocitron**).
- **The system**: the system's repository on GitHub, [BriocheMasquee/sotdl](https://github.com/BriocheMasquee/sotdl).
- **Sample data**: the demonstration entities in this module (ancestry, paths, items, spells, creatures…) are **invented** and provided **for tutorial purposes only**.
:::

### Notices

::: {.regles .cadre}
- *Shadow of the Demon Lord* is a creation of **Robert J. Schwalb**, published by [Schwalb Entertainment](https://schwalbentertainment.com). This module and the system it accompanies are **free, unofficial fan projects**, made with the author's agreement on the condition of reproducing no element of the game.
- This module **contains no rule, text or illustration** from the game. Game content (ancestries, paths, spells, creatures, rules…) is added to your library from the books you own.
- *Encounter+* is an application by **QBit** (www.encounter.plus), created by Juraj; this module is not affiliated with QBit.
:::

### Version and language

This module (**Help SotDL**) is the English version of **Aide OSD**, written separately rather than translated word for word. Both can be downloaded from the system's **recommended content**.

![The system's recommended content](images/recommends.webp){width=900}
name: Credits and notices

content:
# Character sheet

The interactive sheet is a web page served by Encounter+: it **creates** the character step by step, **levels it up**, and is used **in play** (rolls, damage, spells, rest). It reads the entities in your library and writes into the Character entity.

###### Where to go

| I want to… | Page |
|---|---|
| See what the sheet looks like | [Overview](overview) |
| Create a character | [Character creation](create) |
| Go up a level | [Level up](level-up) |
| Attack, cast a spell, use a talent | [Play](play) |
| Handle damage, afflictions, rest | [Damage, afflictions, rest](states) |
| Know what the library must contain | [Prepare your library](prepare) |
name: Character sheet

content:
## Overview

### Opening the sheet

::: {.regles .cadre}
- **From the GM card**: the **Open sheet** button under the level seal. For a new character, the button is **Start character creation**.
- **By address**: `/character/<character slug>`, from the game's web server, in a browser.
:::

![The character sheet open on the Actions tab](images/fiche-vue-ensemble.webp){width=1600}

### The header

###### The elements of the header

| Element | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Level seal** | Shows the level. |
| **Create / level-up button** | A contextual button under the seal that starts character creation or the level up. It turns red, with the number of remaining choices, when choices or rolls are still to be made to complete the level up. |
| **Attributes and characteristics** | Final, calculated values. The button under each attribute makes a test; right-click or long press: boon or bane. |
| **Damage** | The **−** and **+** buttons on each side of the bar heal or inflict 1 damage. Tapping the bar opens a window to type an amount directly, then **Heal** or **Take**. The **wounded** mark is always printed in the middle of the bar. |
| **Insanity, Corruption, Luck, Madness, Darkness marks** | **Insanity**: boxes to tick (or **−** / **+** and a gauge when the maximum is large). **Corruption**: **−** / **+**. **Luck**, **Madness** and **Darkness marks**: switches. |
| **State pills** | One pill per current affliction; **+ Affliction** adds one (see [Damage, afflictions, rest](states)). |
| **Fate banner** | Appears when the character is down; the state and the word **Down** are links to the Rule entity (see [Damage, afflictions, rest](states)). |

### The five tabs

###### What each tab contains

| Tab | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Actions** | Attacks of the equipped weapons, list of actions, **Rest and healing**. |
| **Magic** | Traditions and spells, with their uses. |
| **Talents** | Talents received and chosen, sorted by origin (ancestry, transformation, paths), plus **Other talents**. |
| **Bag** | Money, encumbrance, equipped items and bag items. |
| **Character** | Identity, languages and professions, transformation, complication, history, story, **Calculations**. |

### Editing the sheet

- **✎ Edit** opens a list for editing; **✓ Done** closes it.
- When offline, the sheet says so and **refuses** changes.
- The rolls made from the sheet are named, colored dice: test, attack, damage, fate.
- The **colored 3D dice** only animate in the app; in the sheet opened in a browser (web client), the roll is still made and its result shown, without a 3D die.

### The Character tab: calculations

The **Calculations** section shows, for each characteristic and each attribute, the final value and how it was obtained. The three columns on the right are **editable fields**: this is where you correct the sheet without touching the original entities.

###### Columns of the Calculations section

| Column | Characteristics | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| **Calc.** | Final value, used by the sheet and the card. | Same. |
| **Base** | Adjustable base value. | Same. |
| **Bonus** | Manual bonus added. | — |
| **Anc.** | — | Bonus to the attribute, fed by the ancestry (the **Adjust attributes** creation step writes +1 / −1 here). |
| **Forced** | Imposed value: it replaces the calculation. | Same. |

A small formula to the left of each line recalls where the result comes from.

![The Character tab and its Calculations section](images/fiche-perso-calculs.webp){width=1600}
name: Overview

content:
## Character creation

### Getting started

1. In the library, add a **Character** entity (the **+**), type **only the name** of the character in the **Name** field, then confirm.
2. Open the character card: the **Start character creation** button replaces **Open sheet**.
3. In the sheet, the button under the level seal becomes **Create the character**: it opens the **Character creation** window.

![The GM card button for a new character](images/creation-bouton.webp){width=1200}

### The principle

- The window lists **steps**; each can be **done**, **skipped** or **undone**.
- Rolls (attributes, starting dice, resources) are **made in the window**.
- **Finish creation** closes the window: the character stays at level 0, and the novice path is chosen at level 1.

### The steps

The steps are arranged in two frames: **Ancestry** (what depends on the chosen ancestry) and **Other options**, open from the start.

![The creation window: steps to do](images/creation-fenetre.webp){width=1200}

###### Steps in the Ancestry frame

| Step | Appears | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Ancestry** | Always (required) | Applies the values of the Ancestry entity and opens the steps that depend on it. |
| **Attributes**: rolls, or fixed values OR rolls | If the ancestry is not set to “fixed values” | Rolls the attributes, or lets you choose between fixed values and rolls. |
| **Attributes +1** | Depending on the ancestry | Tick the number of attributes wanted. |
| **Language**, **Profession**, **Language OR profession** | Depending on the ancestry's switches | Choose from the library (Language rules). |
| **Size** | If the ancestry offers several values | Choose the size. |
| **Starting Insanity / Corruption** | If the ancestry sets them to “variable” | Rolls the dice formula. |

###### Steps in the Other options frame

| Step | Appears | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Transformation** (optional) | Always | Adds a transformation. |
| **Insanity / Corruption from the transformation** | If the transformation sets them to Variable mode | A roll step like the ancestry's: the result is shown, can be undone, and is added to the starting value. |
| **Starting option 1/2 and 2/2** | Always | A profession, or another language, or reading a known language. |
| **Starting equipment** | Always | A roll of [3d6](</roll/3d6[Generic]/Starting equipment/check>), then a pointer to the resources table. |
| **Interesting thing** | Always | A roll of [1d6](</roll/1d6[Generic]/Interesting thing: table/check>) (table) then [1d20](</roll/1d20[Generic]/Interesting thing: result/check>) (result), with a pointer to the table. |
| **Adjust attributes** (optional) | Always | One attribute +1, another −1. |
| **Complication** (optional) | Always | Choose a complication. |

Steps marked “optional” can be skipped.

### The starting rolls

The starting Insanity and Corruption rolls (the ancestry's dice formula) are made from the window, with purple (Insanity) and green (Corruption) dice. The result is written straight into the sheet. **A three-sided die has no 3D die in *Encounter+*.**

### Received automatically

As soon as the ancestry is chosen, the sheet fills in on its own: fixed attributes, starting languages and professions, traits, starting values (Insanity, Corruption). The **Received automatically** summary lists them.

### Going back

- Each completed step can be **undone** from its line: it goes back to “to do”.
- Removing a **transformation** also undoes the choices made thanks to it (attributes, language, profession, spell…).
- Removing the **ancestry** does **not** undo its steps: languages, professions and adjustments already entered must be undone by hand (the sheet reminds you when you confirm).
name: Character creation

content:
## Level up

The **Level up** button sits under the level seal and shows, when relevant, the number of choices to make (“n choices to make”). It opens the **Level up** window.

![The level-up window](images/montee-niveau-fenetre.webp){width=1200}

### The window

The window only shows the **target level**, plus the choices still to make from previous levels and the **Other options** frame. Moving to the next level replaces the content, up to level 10 (the maximum). **At level 10**, the **Level up** button disappears.

###### Areas of the window

| Area | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Received automatically** | Bonuses and talents the level grants on its own. |
| **To choose** | The steps the player must go through. |
| **Other options** | Optional, not counted in “choices to make”: purse, interesting things. |
| **Go to level n** | Confirms. The button shows the choices that remain. |

Each completed step can be **undone**: it is listed in the **Received automatically** area or among the choices made, with a cross **✕** on the right; clicking the cross undoes the step, which goes back to “to do”. Removing a **path** does not undo its steps: the sheet reminds you when you confirm.

### The paths

###### Path choices

| Level | Choice |
|---|---|
| 1 | Novice path |
| 3 | Expert path |
| 7 | Master path, **or** second expert path (three white buttons: Undo, Master path, Second expert path); the sheet's frame is then titled **2nd expert path**. |

### The choices offered

They come from the **options ticked in the entity forms** (ancestry, transformation, path): the sheet never deduces anything from the text.

###### Step types

| Step | What the player does |
|---|---|
| **Attributes +1** | Ticks the number of attributes indicated. |
| **A language / a profession / a language OR a profession** | Chooses from the library. |
| **Language abilities** | Ticks, for each known language, what the level allows: spoken, read, written. |
| **Discover a tradition** | Chooses a tradition; a **rank 0 spell** from that tradition follows. |
| **Learn a spell** | Chooses a spell from a tradition already known. |
| **A tradition OR a spell** | Only one of the two. |
| **Talents** | Chooses among the level's “Talents (choice)”. |
| **Talent OR magic** | One choice for the whole level: a talent, or magic. |

### Lowering the level

If you make a mistake, a level can be lowered: do it in the character's form, by selecting the level to go back to. The next time the sheet opens, it lists what will be removed and asks you to **Confirm the decrease**, or offers **Restore level n**. The choices and automatic grants from the higher levels are undone.

### Transformation at any time

A transformation is added or removed from the **Character** tab. Removing it undoes the level choices it had given.
name: Level up

content:
## Play

### Rolls

All roll buttons work the same way: **a click** makes a normal roll; **right-click or long press** opens the choice **Normal roll**, **Boon**, **Bane**. The dice are named and colored (test, attack, damage, fate). An **encumbered** character automatically takes a bane on Strength and Agility rolls: the sheet says so on the roll.

### Actions tab

###### What to do in the Actions tab

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| Choose my turn | The pill under the paths, in the header: each click goes from **Not chosen** to **⚡ Fast turn**, then **⏳ Slow turn**, then back to **Not chosen**. The GM sees it on the card and in the combat tracker. |
| Attack | Click the **attack** button of the equipped weapon, then the **damage** button. |
| Shoot at range | Same: the matching **ammunition** is shown under the weapon, and each roll uses one. |
| Take an action | Open a line of the action list; **+ Action** adds one from the library. |
| Rest | The **Rest and healing** section (see [Damage, afflictions, rest](states)). |

![Actions tab: equipped weapons, attack and damage rolls](images/fiche-actions.webp){width=1600}

### Magic tab

###### What to do in the Magic tab

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| Add a tradition or a spell | **+ Tradition**, **+ Spell**: pickers that search the library. |
| Filter the spells | The tradition buttons at the top of the tab. |
| Track my castings | The uses counter of each spell. |

![Magic tab: traditions, spells and uses](images/fiche-magie.webp){width=1600}

### Talents tab

###### What to do in the Talents tab

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| Use a limited talent | Tick a box of the talent's uses counter. |
| Read a talent | Open its line. |
| Add a free talent | **+ Talent**: it is filed under **Other talents**. |

![Talents tab: talents sorted by origin](images/fiche-talents.webp){width=1600}

### Bag tab

###### What to do in the Bag tab

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| Equip | **Equip** / **Equipped** on the item. |
| See encumbrance | The **Encumbrance** gauge shows the total against Strength (“8 / 10”). Beyond Strength, the **Encumbered** mention appears and Strength and Agility rolls take a bane; beyond double, the mention becomes **Too heavy**. |
| Track a dose | The item's uses counter (checkboxes). |
| Remove an item | Bring its **quantity** to 0: the sheet offers to remove it. |

![Bag tab: money, equipped items and encumbrance](images/fiche-sac.webp){width=1600}

### Character tab

###### What to do in the Character tab

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| Read the character's identity | The **Identity** section (ancestry, paths, age, religion). |
| Manage languages and professions | **+ Language**, **+ Profession**; the **Spoken**, **Read**, **Written** boxes are ticked on each language. |
| See or remove the transformation, the complication | The **Transformation** and **Complication** sections. |
| See how a result is calculated | The **Calculations** section (see [Overview](overview)). |

![Character tab: identity, languages and professions, transformation, complication](images/fiche-perso.webp){width=1600}

### What the sheet calculates on its own

###### Automatic calculations

| Data | Calculated from |
|---|---|
| **Defense** | Equipped armor (otherwise ancestry or Agility), equipped shield, path and transformation bonuses. A path's fixed defense overrides the armor. |
| **Health** | Reference attribute and ancestry bonus, Corruption penalty, level and path bonuses. |
| **Uses of a talent** | Number given + Power if ticked + level if ticked + talents that modify it. |
| **Uses of a spell** | The spell's rank and the character's Power. |
| **Ammunition** | Ammunition items in the bag with the same type as the weapon. |
| **Encumbrance** | Number of items (each item counts for its **quantity**, with no weight) compared with Strength. |
name: Play

content:
## Damage, afflictions, rest

### Damage

The sheet counts **damage taken**, not hit points left. When it reaches Health, the character is **down**.

###### Damage buttons

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Take 1 damage** / **Heal 1 damage** | Adjusts the total by one point. |
| **Edit damage** | Type a value. |
| **Wounded** mark | Always printed in the middle of the bar. |

### Down and the fate roll

When damage reaches Health, the sheet **adds the afflictions on its own** that the rules provide for a downed character (if they exist in the library as **Rule** entities of type **Affliction**) and shows a **banner** under the damage bar. The label of the state in the banner, like the word **Down** on the bar, is a **link to the matching Rule entity**.

###### States of the banner

| State shown | Button | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Incapacitated** | **Fate roll** | Round counter (n/3), one roll per round. |
| **Dying** | **Fate roll** | |
| **Unconscious** | **Roll the unconsciousness time** ([1d3](</roll/1d3[Fate]/Unconsciousness time/check>) hours) | The result is written in the banner (“Unconscious · 2 h”). |
| **Dead** | — | End of tracking. |

###### What the sheet does on its own

| Event | Automatic effect |
|---|---|
| Going down | Adds the starting afflictions. |
| Fate roll | Applies the result the rules provide, adds or removes the afflictions concerned and announces it in a message. |
| Three rounds with no effect | The character becomes **Unconscious**. |
| Leaving the down state (healing) | Removes the afflictions the sheet added. |

::: {.regles .cadre}
- **Waking up**: the GM **removes the Unconscious affliction** (pill, afflictions window or combat tracker). The sheet then heals 1 damage, adds the next affliction the rules provide and clears the banner.
- The sheet only removes the afflictions **it added**: an affliction that came from elsewhere stays with the GM.
- There is no automatic death when damage is taken while the character is down: the GM decides.
- Afflictions are added when the sheet or the card refreshes: if the damage comes from the combat tracker's bar, they appear as soon as a sheet or a card is open.
:::

![The fate banner of a downed character](images/bandeau-destinee.webp){width=1000}

### Afflictions

###### Managing afflictions

| I want to… | I do… |
|---|---|
| See the current afflictions | The pills in the header. When there are too many, the **+n** pill opens the **Current afflictions** window, which lists them all. |
| Read an affliction | Click its pill: the window shows the rule's text, with **Close**, **See rule** and **Remove**. |
| Add one | **+ Affliction**: the list comes from the **Rule** entities of type **Affliction** in the library. |
| Remove one | Click the pill, then **Remove**. |

An affliction added on the sheet also appears in the **combat tracker**, provided the system recognizes it: otherwise the sheet shows “This affliction isn't linked to the system yet” and the GM must update the links.

### Rest

The **Rest and healing** section of the **Actions** tab carries the **Rest** link (“at most once per 24 h”), which offers two durations.

###### Rest

| Rest | Effect |
|---|---|
| **8-hour rest** or **24-hour rest** | Heals according to the healing rate; resets the uses of talents. |
| **Meditate** switch | Also recovers the uses of spells. |

The sheet asks for confirmation before resting.

![Rest and healing](images/repos.webp){width=926}
name: Damage, afflictions, rest

content:
## Prepare your library

The sheet is **empty of game content**: it reads your library. If something is missing, it **says so**.

###### What the sheet expects

| To… | The library needs | If it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| Choose an ancestry | An **Ancestry** entity | Nothing to choose. |
| Choose paths, transformation, complication | **Path**, **Transformation**, **Complication** entities | The step stays empty. |
| Add a language | **Rule** entities of type **Language** | “No Language rule in the library: create them first.” |
| Add an affliction | **Rule** entities of type **Affliction** | “No Affliction rule in the library.” |
| Add an action | **Rule** entities of type **Action** | “No actions: add some from the Action rules.” |
| Add a spell or a tradition | **Spell** entities | Missing automatic spells are reported to the player. |
| Fill the bag | **Item** entities | The bag stays empty. |
| Starting equipment, interesting things | The matching tables (**Table** entities) | The sheet points to a table you must supply. |

### Good to know

::: {.regles .cadre}
- **Linked rules** (an ancestry's starting languages, for instance) are read from the Rule entity: renaming or deleting the rule breaks the link.
- The **rank 0 spells** after a tradition come from the Spell entities: the rank must be filled in.
- **Ammunition** must have the same type as the weapon to be recognized.
:::
name: Prepare your library

content:
# GM side

The GM does not have to open the full sheet: the **character card** (quick reading, rolls, adjustments) and the *Encounter+* **combat window** are enough.

###### What the GM uses

| I want to… | Page |
|---|---|
| Follow a player character at a glance | [The character card](gm-card) |
| Read and roll a creature, an NPC, a vehicle | [Creature views](creature-views) |
| Run a fight: initiative, damage, afflictions | [Combat tracker and initiative](combat-tracker) |
| Set up the system: language, units, combat, images | [System settings](system-settings) |
name: GM side

content:
## The character card

The card is the **quick view** of a Character: it follows the sheet in real time, lets you make some rolls and adjust some values without opening the full sheet. The **Open sheet** button leads to the interactive sheet.

![The GM card of a character](images/carte-mj-personnage.webp){width=1030}

### What it shows

###### Sections of the card

| Section | Contents | Possible actions |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity** | Ancestry, complication, level. | — |
| **Paths** | Paths and levels (novice, expert, master, second path). | — |
| **Attributes** | STR, AGI, INT, WIL, PER. | Rolls. |
| **Characteristics** | Defense, Health and damage, Speed, Size, Power, healing rate. | — |
| **Mind** | Insanity, Corruption, Madness, marks. | Buttons to raise or lower. |
| **Magic** | Spells by rank, uses spent. | — |
| **Attacks** | Attacks of the equipped weapons. | Rolls. |
| **Afflictions** | Current afflictions. | **+ Affliction**. |
| **Purse** | Money. | — |

The card shows the **turn** chosen by the player (**⚡ Fast turn**, **⏳ Slow turn** or **Not chosen**): a click on the pill goes to the next choice, so the GM can correct it. It also shows **Luck**, **Religion** and, if the character is down, the **fate** banner with the same roll as the sheet and the same links to the rules.

### The card's rolls

A roll opens a menu: **Normal roll**, **Boon**, **Bane**, plus **Private roll** to hide the result from the players.

### A new character

For a level 0 character whose creation is not finished, the card becomes a **welcome card** with the big **Start character creation** button.
name: The character card

content:
## Creature views

Creature, NPC and Vehicle each have a **reading view** that builds their card from the form: nothing is typed on the card itself.

![A creature card](images/carte-creature.webp){width=1018}

### Anatomy

###### The bands of a card

| Band | Contains | Comes from the field |
|---|---|---|
| **Black banner** | Name, difficulty (creature) or price (vehicle). | Name, Difficulty / Price |
| **Red band** | Descriptors, fear level, size. | Descriptors, Frightening / terrifying, Size |
| **Values** | Attributes with modifier, Perception, Defense, Health, Speed. | Numeric fields and alternative texts |
| **Lists** | Traits, attacks, special attacks and actions, magic, end of the round. | Lists of the form |
| **Foot** | Description, source. | Common fields |

### What can be clicked

- The **modifier** of each attribute rolls a twenty-sided die with that modifier (a die named “Test”, like the system's other rolls).
- Each **attack** that has a bonus makes its attack roll, with the boons and banes entered; the damage in parentheses after an attack are rolls named after the attack.
- A **link** in a text (spell, rule, creature) opens the entity it points to.

### Before placing a creature in an encounter

::: {.regles .cadre}
- **Defense** is filled in (value or alternative text): it appears in the combat window.
- **Health** is filled in: it sets the threshold at which the creature goes down.
- Each attack has its **Attack bonus**, otherwise it is shown as plain text.
- For an attack's damage die to take its color, write it in the attack's **text** as a named roll link: `([1d6](</roll/1d6[Damage]/Bite/damage>))` (see [Writing in Markdown](index-markdown)). Written plainly (`(1d6)`), the roll is made with *Encounter+*'s default color.
- A vehicle without Defense counts as **5**.
:::
name: Creature views

content:
## Combat tracker and initiative

The combat window is *Encounter+*'s own; the system supplies it with each combatant's **bars**, **detail lines** and **afflictions**.

![The combat window with characters and creatures](images/suivi-combat.webp){width=1010}

### What the system adds to each combatant

###### Lines of the combat tracker

| Combatant | Bar | Detail line |
|---|---|---|
| **Character** | **Damage**: a bar of damage taken, up to Health. | Defense, Perception and, if chosen, the turn (fast or slow). |
| **Creature**, **NPC** | **Damage**, like the character. | Defense (value or alternative text). |
| **Vehicle** | Ordinary health bar. | Defense (value or alternative text). |

The bar is **full when the combatant goes down**: the threshold is the sheet's Health. A character is treated as an ally (“friendly”) in the combat window.

### Afflictions

In the combat window, the **states** menu offers the **Rule** entities of type **Affliction** from the library. For a **Character**, an affliction added in the tracker appears on the sheet and the card, and the other way round.

::: {.regles .cadre}
- An affliction is only linked to the character if the system **knows** it: after adding an affliction rule, the GM must update the affliction links.
- Otherwise the sheet shows “This affliction isn't linked to the system yet”.
:::

### Initiative

Initiative is handled by Encounter+; the system only changes its **settings**, in the **system settings** (**Combat Tracker** group).

###### Combat settings

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Auto-Roll Initiative** | Who rolls initiative automatically. Default: hostile and neutral combatants. |
| **Group Initiative By** | Groups combatants by the chosen criterion. |
| **Re-Roll Initiative Every Round** | A new roll for everyone at the start of each round. |
| **Combatant Image** | Chooses the image shown for each combatant. |

The other system settings are described in [System settings](system-settings).

### A fight, step by step

1. Add characters and creatures to the encounter: the bars and detail lines appear.
2. Roll initiative (according to the **Auto-Roll Initiative** setting). The order is then managed directly by the GM: **drag the cards** of the initiative window into the order wanted, according to the players' choice (slow turn or fast turn).
3. During the fight: damage on the bar, afflictions through the states menu, rolls from the cards.
4. A downed character: the **fate** banner appears on their sheet and card, and the matching afflictions are added (they also appear in the tracker). To wake them, remove their **Unconscious** affliction.
name: Combat tracker and initiative

content:
## System settings

The system has its own settings, opened from *Encounter+*'s **system settings**. They mostly concern the GM: language of the labels, units, combat management and list images.

![The combat management settings](images/reglages-combat.webp){width=922}

### What can be set

###### The groups of settings

| Group | Setting | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| **Locale** | **Language** | The language of the system's labels (sheet, cards, windows). |
| | **Measurement** | The units displayed. |
| **Combat Tracker** | **Auto-Roll Initiative** | Who rolls initiative automatically. Default: hostile and neutral combatants. |
| | **Group Initiative By** | The grouping criterion for combatants in the initiative window. |
| | **Re-Roll Initiative Every Round** | A new initiative for everyone at the start of each round. |
| | **Combatant Image** | The image shown for each combatant. |
| **Interface** | **Default List Image** | The image of entity lists. |
| | **Creature List Image**, **… of characters** | The same setting, specific to each entity type. |

### Good to know

::: {.regles .cadre}
- The **combat** settings are *Encounter+*'s own: the system only offers them in its **Combat Tracker** group (see [Combat tracker and initiative](combat-tracker)).
- With the initiative order, the GM arranges the tracker's cards; the **fast** or **slow** turn chosen by the player appears next to their Perception.
- The field of each setting is described in the index: [Settings](index-settings).
:::
name: System settings

content:
# Entity index

One page per entity. Every page follows the same plan:

::: {.regles .cadre}
1. **The fields**, section by section: the exact label and what the field does.
2. **Imported or calculated automatically**: what the character sheet, the card or the combat tracker pick up without asking.
3. **Worth remembering**: the most common pitfalls.
:::

###### How to read the tables

| Mention | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | The field is not filled in: nothing is shown or calculated (unless stated). |
| **Display** | The field only appears in the reading view. |
| **Calculation** | The character sheet or the card uses it. |
| **Switch** | A checkbox: the sheet **never** deduces a choice from text, only from switches and numbers. |

###### The index pages

| Entity | Page |
|---|---|
| Character | [Character](index-character) |
| Creature and NPC | [Creature](index-creature) |
| Ancestry | [Ancestry](index-ancestry) |
| Path | [Path](index-path) |
| Transformation | [Transformation](index-transformation) |
| Item | [Item](index-item) |
| Spell | [Spell](index-spell) |
| Complication | [Complication](index-complication) |
| Vehicle | [Vehicle](index-vehicle) |
| Rule | [Rule](index-rule) |
| Table | [Table](index-table) |
| System settings | [Settings](index-settings) |
| Shared blocks | [Talents and level choices](index-talents) · [Links and rolls](index-links-dice) |
| Writing | [Writing in Markdown](index-markdown) (reference for authors) |
name: Entity index

content:
## Character

The character **contains copies** of its ancestry, paths, transformation and complication, plus its languages, magic and bag. Its interactive sheet and its card read this data; attributes and characteristics are **calculated**.

###### Identity

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Level** | Calculation: decides the benefits received and the choices offered. Lowering it triggers the decrease confirmation. |
| **Turn type** | Choice: **Not chosen** (default), **Fast turn**, **Slow turn**. Display: the sheet (header pill, under the paths), the GM card and the combat tracker pick it up. Both the player and the GM can change it; it does not reset by itself. |
| **Ancestry** (reference) | Import: copies the Ancestry entity into the character. |
| **Transformation** (reference) | Import: copies the transformation; removing it undoes its level choices. |
| **Complication** (reference) | Import: copies the complication and its traits. |
| **Complication › Note a choice** / **Player's choice** | Display: the player notes their choice for a trait there. |
| **Novice Path**, **Expert Path**, **Master Path**, **Second expert path** | Import: copies the path; the sheet applies its bonuses level by level. |

###### Languages

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Rules** (reference) | Import: the language is a Rule entity of type Language. |
| **Spoken**, **Read**, **Written** | Switches: what the character can do in that language. |

###### Magic and bag

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Traditions** | List of known traditions. |
| **Spells** (reference) | Import: copy of the spell. |
| **Override maximum uses** | Calculation: replaces the calculated maximum number of uses. |
| **Items** (reference) | Import: copy of the item; **Quantity** counts the copies. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### What the sheet calculates on its own

| Data | Source |
|---|---|
| Attributes, Defense, Health, Speed, Perception, Power, Size | Ancestry, paths, transformation, levels, equipped armor; corrected by **Base / Bonus / Forced** in the **Character** tab. |
| Insanity, Corruption | Starting values of the ancestry and the transformation. |
| Uses of talents and spells | See [Talents and level choices](index-talents). |
| Encumbrance | Bag compared with Strength: automatic bane on Strength and Agility rolls. |

### Worth remembering

- The copy is **frozen**: editing the Ancestry entity does not change a character already created.
- A character is normally created **from the interactive sheet** (see [Character creation](create)).
name: Character

content:
## Creature and NPC

The **NPC** entity uses exactly the same form (it extends Creature); it has its own collection.

###### General

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Difficulty** | Display: black banner “Difficulty n”. |
| **Descriptors** | Display: red band under the name. |
| **Frightening / terrifying** | Display: fear level, with the feminine form if **Feminine form** is ticked. Terrifying overrides Frightening. |
| **Size** (list) | Display and calculation: red band, size category. |

###### Attributes and characteristics

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Strength, Agility, Intellect, Will, Perception** | Display: value and modifier (value − 10); the modifier rolls a twenty-sided die. **Empty**: a dash. |
| **Special Senses** | Display after Perception. |
| **Defense** + **alternative text** | Display: the text replaces the value. Feeds the combat tracker line. |
| **Armor** | Display in parentheses after Defense. |
| **Health** + **alternative text** | Display. **The value sets the threshold for going down** in the combat tracker. |
| **Insanity, Corruption** | Display after Health. |
| **Speed**, **Special Movement Traits** | Display. |

###### Lists

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Traits, immunities, vulnerabilities** | Simple talents (name + description), at the top of the card. |
| **Attack Options** | One line per attack (see below). |
| **Special Attacks**, **Special Actions** | Simple talents, under their subheading; hidden if the list is empty. |
| **Magic**: **Power**, **Traditions and known spells** | Display; spells are text: link them by hand (see [Links and rolls](index-links-dice)). |
| **End of the Round** | End-of-round effects, name + description. |

###### An attack line

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Bold. |
| **Type and range** | In parentheses, lowercase. Enter **without parentheses**. |
| **Attack bonus** | Calculation: creates the attack roll. **Empty**: the line becomes a simple trait. |
| **Boons** / **Banes** | Calculation: six-sided dice added to the roll; boons win. |
| **Rest of the attack or description** | Display: damage and effects. A die written plainly stays purple: write it as a named roll link (see [Links and rolls](index-links-dice)). |

### Imported or calculated automatically

What the sheet, the card or the combat tracker pick up without asking.

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Combat tracker** | Damage bar (threshold = Health), “Defense” line. |
| **Creature list** | Difficulty, descriptors, fear, size. |
| **Card** | The whole form, arranged in bands. |

### Worth remembering

- Does each attack have its **Attack bonus**? Otherwise it is text.
- Range **without parentheses**.
- Special values (variable Defense): in the **alternative text** fields.
name: Creature and NPC

content:
## Ancestry

An Ancestry entity describes what a people grants at creation, then at certain levels. The interactive sheet applies what it finds in the **structured fields** (numbers, switches, lists); a free text field only displays.

###### Attributes

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Starting attribute values** | Chooses the mode: **Classic** (fixed values applied), **Variant** (the player chooses fixed values or rolls), **Variable** (imposed rolls). |
| **Strength, Agility, Intellect, Will** (numbers) | Calculation: fixed values (Classic and Variant modes). |
| **Formulas** (text) | Calculation: rolls, for example `1d3+8` (Variant and Variable modes). |
| **Number of attributes with a +1 bonus** | The **Attributes +1** creation step. |
| **Attribute choices**, **No adjustments allowed** | Display only (Variable mode). |

###### Characteristics

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Perception bonus** | Calculation: added to Perception. |
| **Fixed Defense** | Calculation: replaces Defense by Agility. **Empty**: Defense follows Agility. |
| **Health**: attribute, bonus, penalty per Corruption point | Calculation. **Empty**: based on Strength. |
| **Size** | Calculation: unless the player adjusts it. |
| **Speed** | Calculation: starting Speed. |
| **Insanity**, **Corruption**: **Fixed** / **Variable** | Calculation: starting value; in Variable, a roll at creation. |

###### Languages, professions, traits

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Languages and Professions** (text) | Display (view and origin frame). |
| **Grants 1 language**, **Grants 1 profession**, **Language OR profession** | Switches: creation steps. |
| **Starting languages** | Import: language (Rule) + Spoken / Read / Written written into the sheet. |
| **Starting professions** | Import: name + optional detail. |
| **Traits, immunities, vulnerabilities** | Import: talents (see [Talents and level choices](index-talents)). |

###### Advantages by level

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Powerful Ancestry** | Switch: adds levels 1, 2, 5 and 8 (level 4 is always there). |
| **Attributes**, **Characteristics** (per level) | Calculation: numeric bonuses; **Other** for what cannot be expressed as numbers. |
| **Level Options** | Display. |
| **Choices** (attributes, language and profession, magic, talents) | Switches and numbers: level-up steps. |
| **Automatic spells**, **Automatic talents**, **Talents (choice)** | Import when the level is reached. |
| **Ancestry tables** | Displayed at the bottom of the entity. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| When | What the sheet picks up |
|---|---|
| Ancestry chosen | Fixed attributes, Perception, Defense, Health, Size, Speed, starting Insanity and Corruption, starting languages and professions, traits. |
| Each level reached | The level's bonuses, automatic talents and spells, choice steps. |

### Worth remembering

- Every choice wanted at creation has its **switch**.
- Starting languages and professions: in the **lists**, not only in the text.
- Advantages at levels 1, 2, 5, 8: tick **Powerful Ancestry**.
name: Ancestry

content:
## Path

A Path entity describes what a character receives by following a course, level by level. The interactive sheet reads it for each level reached.

###### Type and levels

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Path type** | Decides the levels offered: **Novice** (1, 2, 5, 8), **Expert** (3, 6, 9), **Master** (7, 10). Changing the type hides the levels (the data stays). |
| **Category** | Experts and masters only: a list specific to the type; shown in parentheses after the type. |
| **Other talents** | Switch: adds a section (**Name** + list of simple talents) at the end of the entity. Text only: no uses, no choices. |

###### Contents of each level

Same form as the levels of an [Ancestry](index-ancestry).

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Attributes**, **Characteristics** | Calculation: numeric bonuses (Perception, Defense, **Fixed Defense**, Health, Speed, Power, Insanity, Corruption, Size bonus); **Other** for the rest. |
| **Languages and Professions**, **Level Options** | Display. |
| **Choices** (attributes, language and profession, magic, talents) | Switches and numbers: level-up steps. |
| **Automatic spells**, **Automatic talents**, **Talents (choice)** | Import when the level is reached. |
| **Path tables** | Displayed at the bottom of the entity. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| When | What the sheet picks up |
|---|---|
| Level 1, 3, 7: choice of path | Copy of the path into the character (novice, expert, master or second expert path). |
| Each level of the path | Numeric bonuses, automatic talents and spells, choice steps. |
| **Fixed Defense** | It overrides the equipped armor. |

### Worth remembering

- The **Path type** drives everything: check it first.
- A talent with a counter needs its **Number of uses**.
name: Path

content:
## Transformation

A change added to a character **at any time**. The sheet applies its values on top of those of the ancestry, levels and paths; removing it undoes its level choices.

###### Attributes (for each of the four)

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Remove attribute** | Calculation: the attribute is no longer calculated (hides the next two fields). |
| **Relative value** | Calculation: added to the attribute. |
| **Replace with** | Calculation: the attribute becomes this number, **capped at 20**. The player's manual adjustment still takes priority. |

###### Characteristics

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Perception, Defense, Health, Speed bonus** | Calculation: added. |
| **Health penalty per Corruption point** | Calculation: adds to the ancestry's. |
| **Healing rate fixed at 0** | Calculation: imposes 0. |
| **Insanity removed** | Calculation: brings Insanity back to 0. |
| **Insanity added**, **Corruption added**: **Fixed** / **Variable** | Calculation: a value, or a dice formula. In **Variable**, the sheet opens a roll window when the transformation is added and **records the result**, added to the starting value (it is erased if the transformation is removed). |

###### The rest

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Prerequisites** | Display only: the sheet checks nothing. |
| **Traits, immunities, vulnerabilities** | Import: talents (see [Talents and level choices](index-talents)). |
| **Powerful Ancestry** | Switch: adds levels 1, 2, 5 and 8 (level 4 is always there). |
| **Replaces the ancestry's level 4** | Calculation: the **numeric** bonuses of the ancestry's level 4 no longer count (not its talents or choices). |
| **Advantages by Level** | Same principle as an [Ancestry](index-ancestry); level 4 has no Attributes, Insanity, Corruption or Size bonus. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| When | What the sheet picks up |
|---|---|
| Transformation added | Attribute and characteristic changes, Insanity and Corruption added, traits. |
| Levels reached | Bonuses, talents, choices. |
| Removal | The level choices given by the transformation are undone. |

### Worth remembering

- **Relative value** adds; **Replace with** sets.
- If it replaces an ancestry advantage, tick **Replaces the ancestry's level 4**.
name: Transformation

content:
## Item

The **Item Type** field drives the others: choose it **first**. In a character's bag, the sheet reads the type, damage, Defense, doses and ammunition.

###### Fields shown by type

| Field | Shown for |
|---|---|
| **Price**, **Availability** | Armor, weapon, potion, gear, special item. |
| **Gear Type** / **Special Item Type** | Gear / special item. |
| **Uses or doses** | Potion, gear, special item, relic, ammunition. |
| **Armor type**, **Requirements**, **Defense (fixed value)**, **Defense: Agility +** | Armor. |
| **Weapon Type**, **Damage**, **Hands**, **Properties**, **Requirements** | Weapon. |
| **Ammunition type** | Ammunition, or a weapon that uses ammunition. |
| **Game Effects** | Relic (simple talents: name + description). |

###### Effects in the character sheet

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Defense (fixed value)** or **Agility +** | Calculation: the **equipped** armor replaces the ancestry's Defense; a shield adds its bonus. Fixed value **or** Agility bonus, not both. |
| **Damage** | Calculation: the sheet turns it into a roll button. **Empty**: no button. |
| **Hands** | Display under the weapon's name. |
| **Uses ammunition** + **Ammunition type** | Calculation: the sheet looks in the bag for **Ammunition** items of the same type and shows their counter; each roll uses one. |
| **Uses or doses** | Calculation: uses counter (checkboxes) in the bag. A **quantity** of 0 offers to remove the item. |
| **Properties** | Display on one line; the reach and defensive values only appear if the switch is ticked. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Bag** | Equipped / not equipped, quantity, doses. |
| **Actions tab** | One attack line per equipped weapon. |
| **Encumbrance** | Number of items (each counts for its quantity, with no weight) compared with Strength. |

### Worth remembering

- To create ammunition: item type **Weapon**, weapon type **Ammunition**, then **Ammunition type**.
- Fill in the doses of items that wear out.
name: Item

content:
## Spell

###### Spell fields

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Tradition** | Display at the top of the view; files the spell in the **Magic** tab. |
| **Dark magic**, **Psychic Tradition**, **Incantation only** | Switches: a mention under the title and an icon near the tradition. |
| **Type** | Attack or Utility. |
| **Rank** | Calculation: from 0 to 10; rank 0 is that of cantrips. |
| **Requirements**, **Target**, **Area of Effect**, **Duration** | Display, each on its own line. |
| **Special Entries** | Simple talents (name + description); an entry that has a name is shown **without a first-line indent**, as in the book. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Magic tab** | The spell appears under its tradition, with a uses counter. |
| **Maximum uses** | Calculation: the spell's rank and the character's Power; **Override maximum uses** (in the character) replaces them. |
| **Automatic spells** of a level | The Spell entities are found by reference; if they are missing, the sheet says so. |

### Worth remembering

- Fill in the **Rank**: without it, the counter cannot be calculated.
name: Spell

content:
## Complication

###### Fields

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Display in capitals. |
| **Description** | Display. |
| **Traits** | List: each trait has a name and a description. |
| **Complication tables** | Displayed at the bottom of the entity. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Creation** | The optional **Complication** step (in **Other options**). The sheet copies the complication and its traits. |
| **Character sheet** | For a trait, **Note a choice** and **Player's choice** let you write your decision. |
name: Complication

content:
## Vehicle

The **Vehicle type** field drives the visible fields. The vehicle **reuses** the lists of the [Creature](index-creature): attack options, special attacks, special actions.

###### Fields shown by type

| Field | Shown for |
|---|---|
| **Price**, **Size**, **Descriptors**, attributes, **Defense**, **Armor**, **Health**, **Space**, **Crew** | All. |
| **Availability** | Ship, war machine. |
| **Maximum speed**, **Cargo** | Vehicle, ship. |
| **Acceleration**, **Deceleration**, **Special Movement Traits** | Vehicle. |
| **Draft**, **Passengers**, **Seaworthiness**, **Handling** | Ship. |
| **Ammunition** | War machine. |

###### Default values and specific rules

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Defense** | **Empty: 5.** |
| **Strength**, **Agility** | **Empty: 0.** |
| **Size** | A **number** (not a list like the creature); gives the size category. |
| **Standard immunities** | Switch: adds a line of immunities whose text depends on the type. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Combat tracker** | Ordinary health bar, “Defense” line. |
| **Vehicle list** | Type and size. |
name: Vehicle

content:
## Rule

A Rule entity carries a **text** and a **type**; the type decides where the sheet, the card or the combat tracker find it. Game content (languages, afflictions, actions…) lives in Rule entities in **your** library: the system contains none.

###### Fields

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Name** | The entity's title; also its name in lists. |
| **Type** | Classifies the rule: **Action**, **Affliction**, **State**, **Danger**, **Movement**, **Mind**, **Language**, **Other**, **Source**. |
| **Description** | Display: the rule's text (Markdown). |
| **Source** | Display: book and page, at the bottom of the entity. |
| **Image** | Shown only for the **Source** type. |
| **Icon** | Used by the combat tracker for an affliction; never shown in the rule's view. |

###### What each type is for

| Type | What the system does with it |
|---|---|
| **Language** | List of choices for starting languages, the **Language** steps and the **Languages** section of the character. |
| **Affliction** | The **+ Affliction** menu of the sheet and the card, states of the combat tracker. |
| **Action** | The **+ Action** list of the **Actions** tab. |
| **State** | Reference entity (down, incapacitated…): **no** combat tracker behavior. |
| **Danger**, **Movement**, **Mind**, **Other** | Reference entities, available through links. |
| **Source** | An entity for a book, cited by the **Source** field of other entities. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Character sheet** | The text of a language or an action is read live from the rule. |
| **Combat tracker** | An affliction only appears there if the system's links were updated after it was created. |

### Worth remembering

- A rule that is **deleted or renamed** breaks the links that point to it.
- An action's rolls are written in its description: see [Links and rolls](index-links-dice).
name: Rule

content:
## Table

The **Table** entity is a type **native to Encounter+**: the system adds no form, only a view.

###### What the view shows

| Element | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Name** | Title. |
| **Roll** + formula | The table's roll button (if a formula is defined). |
| **Source** or **footer** | Display under the title. |
| **Description**, **tables**, **notes** | Display, in order. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| Where | What is picked up |
|---|---|
| **Character creation** | **Starting equipment** and **Interesting thing** point to tables to supply in the library. |
| **Ancestry, path, transformation, complication** | The **Tables** field displays text: it rolls nothing. |
name: Table

content:
## Settings

The **Settings** form is found in the system settings of Encounter+.

###### Fields

| Group | Field | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Locale** | **Language** | Language of the system's labels. |
| | **Measurement** | Units displayed. |
| **Combat Tracker** | **Auto-Roll Initiative** | Who rolls initiative automatically. |
| | **Group Initiative By** | Groups combatants by the chosen criterion. |
| | **Re-Roll Initiative Every Round** | A new roll for everyone at the start of each round. |
| | **Combatant Image** | Image shown for each combatant. |
| **Interface** | **Default List Image** | Image of entity lists. |
| | **Creature List Image**, **… of characters** | The same setting, per entity type. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

No data is imported: these settings apply to the display and to the combat tracker (see [Combat tracker and initiative](combat-tracker)).
name: Settings

content:
## Talents and level choices

The **talent form** is the same everywhere (ancestry, transformation, path). It has two shapes: the **simple talent** (**Name** + **Description**), used by creatures, NPCs, vehicles, relics and “Other talents” sections, and the **talent with uses**.

###### Uses of a talent

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Number of uses** | Calculation: creates a counter on the sheet. **Empty**: no counter. |
| **Add Power** | Calculation: the character's Power is added to the maximum. |
| **Add the character level** | Calculation: the **character's** level is added to the maximum. |
| **Name of the talent changed** + **Extra uses** | Calculation: this talent adds uses to another, designated by its name (capitals, accents and spaces ignored). It must be one of the character's talents. |

Maximum = number of uses + Power (if ticked) + level (if ticked) + talents that modify it. The counter only appears if the number is filled in and the maximum is above 0.

###### Level choices

Each level offers four groups of **switches and numbers**; the sheet draws level-up steps from them.

| Group | Fields | Steps offered |
|---|---|---|
| **Attributes** | **Number of attributes with a +1 bonus** | **Attributes +1**. |
| **Language and profession** | **Grants 1 language**, **Grants 1 profession**, **Language OR profession**, **Abilities for known languages** | Language, profession, or one OR the other; **Language abilities** (spoken, read, written). |
| **Magic** | **Grants 1 tradition**, **Grants 1 spell**, **Tradition OR spell**, **Number of choices to make**, **Cantrip (Magician)** | Tradition, spell, or one OR the other; a rank 0 spell follows each tradition discovered. |
| **Talents** | **Grants 1 talent**, **Number of talents to choose**, **Talent OR magic (one choice only)** | A choice among the level's **Talents (choice)**. |

### Imported or calculated automatically

###### Automatic pickups

| When | What the sheet picks up |
|---|---|
| Level reached | **Automatic talents** and **automatic spells**: received without doing anything. |
| Level up | Steps deduced from the switches; **Talents (choice)**: the player chooses. |

### Worth remembering

- **Grants 1 talent** ticked with an empty **Talents (choice)** list: the sheet shows a warning.
- The sheet **never reads the text** to guess a choice.
name: Talents and level choices

content:
## Links and rolls

###### Links in a text

| To link… | Write | Example |
|---|---|---|
| An entity by its name | `[text](type)` | `[Spell name](spell)` |
| A specific entity (plural, feminine…) | `[text](/type/slug)` | `[the spells](/spell/spell-name)` |
| A rule | `[text](rule)` | `[Rule name](rule)` |
| A module page | `[text](page-slug)` | `[credits](credits)` |

Types: `creature`, `npc`, `spell`, `item`, `vehicle`, `ancestry`, `transformation`, `path`, `complication`, `rule`, `table`. The *slug* is the name without accents, in lowercase, with hyphens.

###### Dice rolls in a text

**Every roll is named**: without a name, *Encounter+* rolls it with its default color (see [Writing in Markdown](index-markdown)).

| To get | Write |
|---|---|
| Damage | `[1d6](</roll/1d6[Damage]/Label/damage>)` |
| An attack | `[+7](</roll/d20[Attack]+7/Label/attack>)` |
| A test | `[+2](</roll/d20[Test]+2/Label/check>)` |
| Any other roll | `[1d6](</roll/1d6[Generic]/Label/check>)` |

Writing rules: the die first (`1d3+8`), formula **without spaces**, the die name's brackets **raw**, the ordinary hyphen `-`, and angle brackets `< >` around the path if the label contains spaces.

###### Reference fields

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Reference** (automatic spells, starting languages, rules) | The sheet looks up the entity pointed to; if it does not exist, it says so. |
| **Choice list** | Value provided by the system: no entity is created. |
| **Source** | A book and a page (whole number), at the bottom of the entity. |
name: Links and rolls

content: ## Writing in Markdown Reference for module and entity authors. Every notation is shown with its **real rendering**: what you see in the **Result** column is written in Markdown on this page. ### Where Markdown is read ###### Entity fields | Field | Markdown | |---|---| | **Description** of all entities | Yes. | | **Tables** (Ancestry, Path, Transformation, Complication) | Yes. | | Names and texts of **talents**, choices, traits, special attacks, spell and relic effects | Yes. | | Fields of a stat block (Armor, Insanity, Corruption, Price…) | Yes: they are inserted into a line of Markdown. | | Title of a collapsible group in a native view | No. | Style classes (`{.class}`) and `:::` blocks are **reserved for module pages**: in an entity, they would be displayed as typed. ### Text ###### Text formatting | Write | Result | |---|---| | `**bold**` | **bold** | | `*italic*` | *italic* | | `~~strikethrough~~` | ~~strikethrough~~ | | `underlined` | underlined | | `highlighted` | highlighted | | `H2O` | H2O | | `x2` | x2 | Underline, highlight, subscript and superscript only exist as **HTML tags**: the shorthand notations of other Markdown flavors are not recognized by *Encounter+*. ###### Notations that do not work | Notation | What you get | Use instead | |---|---|---| | `==text==` | ==text== | `text` | | `~x~` | H~2~O | `x` | | `^x^` | 2^10^ | `x` | | `- [ ] task` | shown as typed | An ordinary list | ### Headings A page title is an **H2**, sections are **H3**, table titles are **H6** followed by a sentence. An **H1** is only used for the title of a part. Every heading gets an anchor. :::::duo ::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ## Page title (H2) ### Section title (H3) #### Level 4 title (H4) ##### Level 5 title (H5) ###### Table title (H6) ``` :::: ::::duo-rendu **Result** #### Level 4 title (H4) ##### Level 5 title (H5) ###### Table title (H6) The H2 and H3 headings of this page are the example. :::: ::::: ### Lists and quotes :::::duo ::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown - a bullet - another bullet 1. a first point 2. a second point > A quote. ``` :::: ::::duo-rendu **Result** - a bullet - another bullet 1. a first point 2. a second point > A quote. :::: ::::: ### Tables The first column starts **at the margin**, with a closing bar at the end of each line. An indented table, or one inside a code fence, becomes raw code. :::::duo ::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ###### Table title | Column A | Column B | |---|---| | One cell | Another | | Again | And again | ``` :::: ::::duo-rendu **Result** ###### Table title | Column A | Column B | |---|---| | One cell | Another | | Again | And again | :::: ::::: ### Links A link's pill takes the **color of its target type**: green (ancestry, path, transformation, complication), purple (spell), gold (item), red (creature, NPC, vehicle), blue (rule, table), brown (module page). For an entity, the **color class** `{.lk-…}` is written right after the link; for a rule, a table or a page, the color comes from the address. ###### Link notations | Target | Write | Result | |---|---|---| | An ancestry, by name | `[Glimmerkin](ancestry){.lk-entity}` | [Glimmerkin](ancestry){.lk-entity} | | A path | `[Peddler](path){.lk-entity}` | [Peddler](path){.lk-entity} | | A transformation | `[Reflection](transformation){.lk-entity}` | [Reflection](transformation){.lk-entity} | | A complication | `[Absent-minded](complication){.lk-entity}` | [Absent-minded](complication){.lk-entity} | | A spell | `[Minute Breeze](spell){.lk-spell}` | [Minute Breeze](spell){.lk-spell} | | An item | `[Ironshod Staff](item){.lk-item}` | [Ironshod Staff](item){.lk-item} | | A creature | `[Attic Prowler](creature){.lk-creature}` | [Attic Prowler](creature){.lk-creature} | | A rule | `[Murmurish](rule)` | [Murmurish](rule) | | A table | `[Daily Finds](table)` | [Daily Finds](table) | | A specific entity (plural, feminine…) | `[the glimmerkin](/ancestry/glimmerkin){.lk-entity}` | [the glimmerkin](/ancestry/glimmerkin){.lk-entity} | | Another page of the module | `[Play](play)` | [Play](play) | | A heading on the same page | `[Dice rolls](#dice-rolls)` | [Dice rolls](#dice-rolls) | | An external address | `[Encounter+](https://www.encounter.plus)` | [Encounter+](https://www.encounter.plus) | The link name is compared without regard to capitals or accents. An entity of **your** library is only found if it exists. A heading's anchor is its text in lowercase, without accents, with hyphens. ### Dice rolls **Every dice roll is named**: the die's name, in raw brackets right after it, gives the 3D die its color. Without a name, *Encounter+* rolls the die with its default color. A roll that fits no category is called **Generic**. ###### Roll notations | To get | Write | Result | |---|---|---| | An attack | `[+7]()` | [+7]() | | Damage | `[1d6]()` | [1d6]() | | A test | `[+2]()` | [+2]() | | A fate roll | `[1d6]()` | [1d6]() | | An Insanity roll | `[1d6]()` | [1d6]() | | A Corruption roll | `[1d6]()` | [1d6]() | | Any other roll | `[1d6]()` | [1d6]() | - Write the die **first**, the modifier next, without spaces: `1d3+8`. - A label with spaces requires **angle brackets** `< >` around the path. - The typographic dash breaks the formula: always write `-`. - The brackets of the die name stay **raw**: encoded (`%5B`), they break the roll. ### Page blocks and extensions Module pages are read by a Markdown engine with extensions. ###### Page extensions | To get | Write | |---|---| | A footnote | `[^1]` then, further down, `[^1]: text` | | A class block | `::: class` … `:::`; nested block: longer fence (`::::`) | | Attributes | `{#id .class width=400}` after a heading, a link or an image | | An image | `![text](images/x.webp){width=400}` | A footnote appears at the end of the page[^1]. [^1]: This is the text of the note. ### Style classes A class goes on a `::: class` block (or `::: {.class}`); a nested block needs a longer fence (`::::`). Classes are **reserved for module pages**. ###### Framed rules block `regles` and `cadre`: a frame of rules, one bullet per trait. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: {.regles .cadre} - **A trait.** Its text. - **Another trait.** Its text. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: {.regles .cadre} - **A trait.** Its text. - **Another trait.** Its text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Black field names `champs`: bold lead-ins of bullets stay black instead of turning red. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: champs - **Field.** Its effect. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: champs - **Field.** Its effect. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Sidebar `sidebar`: a sidebar with a title. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: sidebar #### Sidebar title Sidebar text. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: sidebar #### Sidebar title Sidebar text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Note `note`: an application note, in blue. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: note Note text. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: note Note text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Read-aloud text `read`: a text to read aloud, in italics with a rule. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: read Text to read. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: read Text to read. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Annotation `annotation`: a framed remark, like a quote. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: annotation Annotation text. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: annotation Annotation text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Stat block `statblock`: a stat block: black banner (`####` + ``), red band (italic paragraph), gray bands (`#####`). :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown ::: {.statblock} #### NAME PRICE 5 GP *Descriptors* **Field** value ##### Gray band **Trait.** Text. ::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: {.statblock} #### NAME PRICE 5 GP *Descriptors* **Field** value ##### Gray band **Trait.** Text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Spell `sort`: how a spell is presented: red title, tradition as a pill. :::::::duo ::::::duo-code **Write** ```markdown :::: {.sort} #### NAME Tradition rank 1 **Target.** Text. :::: ``` :::::: ::::::duo-rendu **Result** ::::: {.sort} #### NAME Tradition rank 1 **Target.** Text. ::::: :::::: ::::::: ###### Full-width image `size-cover`: an image at the top of the page, edge to edge. It is written after the image: ```markdown ![text](images/x.webp){.size-cover} ``` ### Worth remembering - In an entity, no classes and no `:::` blocks. - Write dice as named rolls, never plainly. - A table title is an **H6** followed by a sentence.
name: Writing in Markdown
